function: Sensor-aided multi-user beam training: a DNN predicts the beamspace (path AoDs) from camera, LiDAR and position data to select the BS analog RF precoders (pp. 1-2, 8).
system: Downlink MU-MISO OFDM at 60 GHz: BS hybrid array 16x8 (U=2) or 16x16 (U=4) elements, single-antenna UEs; 792 subcarriers at 120 kHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: Supervised multimodal fusion DNN (CNN and fully connected layers) trained with binary cross-entropy plus a proposed supervised soft-contrastive loss; multi-label AoD prediction (pp. 5-7, 9).
data_channel: Raymobtime s008 (training, 2086 scenes) and s009 (testing, 2000 scenes): public ray-tracing channels at 60 GHz in Rosslyn with LiDAR, camera, and UE coordinates (p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained on s008, tested on s009 (same Rosslyn scenario, 60 GHz); U = 2 and U = 4 users; EIRP 0-50 dBm; sensor-modality subsets compared (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Full-CSI digital precoding (upper bound); ideal-beam DFT prediction, stated as best case of the learned framework [27]; ground-truth beamspace oracle; unimodal and no-SSCL ablations (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Achievable sum spectral efficiency (median and 25-75th percentile) versus EIRP, empirical CDF of sum-SE, mean angular distance (MAD), MAE in cosines, and signaling overhead (pp. 7, 10-12).
complexity: none; only signaling overhead is quantified: one SSB (5/64 ms) versus up to 64 SSBs, and the network size is described qualitatively (pp. 11-12).
openness: No code or data release of its own; trains and tests on the public Raymobtime datasets s008/s009 [23], no link given (pp. 1, 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "we use the Raymobtime dataset [23]. This dataset comprises a collection of synthetic ray tracing datasets" - public ray-tracing dataset (60 GHz, Rosslyn), not DeepMIMO or 3GPP; met as another public ray-tracing dataset, for the reviewer to confirm.
q2_support: p. 9: "we use datasets s008 for training our fusion model, while s009 is used for validating the obtained results" - borderline: s009 is another Raymobtime dataset of the same Rosslyn scenario, band and arrays; no new scenario, site, band or array, so counted as a held-out set.
q3_support: p. 10: "framework [27] when extended to MU setting without prediction error" - the beam prediction baseline is the best case of the earlier learned sensor-aided framework [27], an oracle best DFT beam per UE, not a trained model; Full CSI is classical; ablations are variants of the proposed method.
q4_support: p. 11: "the proposed two-stage approach reduces the overhead by the factor of upto 64" - this is signaling overhead (SSB time); no complexity order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime of the DNN is given.
q5_support: p. 1: "Further fueled by the publicly available datasets like Raymobtime [23]" - trains and tests on the public Raymobtime datasets s008 and s009 (p. 9); no own code or data link is given.
notes: PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2406.05300v1, 7 Jun 2024; p. 1). Area 3: the main metric is the sum-SE of MU beamforming (p. 1) and the DNN only predicts path AoDs for precoder selection. q1 and q5 rest on Raymobtime, a public ray-tracing dataset other than DeepMIMO, for the reviewer to confirm. q2 and q3 are borderline and marked 0: s008 to s009 is one benchmark split of the same scenario, and the learned baseline is an oracle bound of [27], not a trained model.
